 The Golden State Warriors superstar may be nearing the final chapter of his illustrious career, but the veteran sharpshooter continues to prove that he remains a dominant force in the NBA this season . Stephen Curry has already reached several significant milestones during the season, and he added another remarkable achievement during Saturday's matchup against the Orlando Magic.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Curry joined an exclusive group featuring Kobe Bryant , James Harden, John Havlicek, LeBron James , Oscar Robertson and Russell Westbrook, becoming just the seventh player in NBA history to record at least 26,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 6,000 assists.
 Additionally, the 38-year-old became the fastest point guard since the NBA-ABA merger to reach 25,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 5,000 assists.

 Curry made a strong impact in the first half alone, finishing with 14 points, four rebounds and four assists. He was highly efficient from the floor, converting five of his six field-goal attempts, including two of three from beyond the arc, while going a perfect 2-of-2 from the free-throw line.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Warriors entered halftime holding a commanding 16-point advantage, with Curry delivering an unbelievable shot to close out the first half. The Warriors superstar has now knocked down at least one three-pointer in 100 consecutive regular-season games. It marks the seventh-longest streak in NBA history and the third-longest of his career.
 Curry continues to serve as the focal point of Golden State's offense, relying on his elite shooting, and playmaking skills to keep the team competitive. Despite the NBA's emergence of a new generation of stars, the Warriors superstar's impact remains irreplaceable.
 Golden State has also demonstrated that it has enough offensive firepower to compete with established Western Conference contenders. However, improving its defensive consistency and maintaining a high level of performance throughout games will be equally important.
